Struct RotationMatrix

A rotation matrix in three dimensions preserves handedness and has a determinant of exactly one. The matrix stores its components in row-major order so that slicing the underlying buffer yields the three basis vectors of the rotated frame in sequence.

Construct the matrix with the guaranteed-orthonormal constructor; the fallible variant rejects inputs whose columns are not unit length within the documented tolerance of the crate.

Signatures

pub struct RotationMatrix {
    basis: [Vector3; 3],
}

Methods

pub fn from_axis_angle(axis: Vector3, radians: f64) -> Self

Builds a rotation about axis by radians, normalizing the axis before use and panicking when the axis degenerates to zero length in the caller frame.

Examples

let frame = RotationMatrix::from_axis_angle(Vector3::UP, std::f64::consts::FRAC_PI_2);
assert!(frame.is_orthonormal());

Rotating the unit up vector by a quarter turn lands on the forward axis, which the assertion checks through the orthonormal predicate of the matrix.
